en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the abuses of Spanish colonial friars in the Philippines.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines serves as the highest tribunal and has the power to interpret the Constitution.
The Philippine eagle, also called the monkey-eating eagle, is a critically endangered bird endemic to the country's forests.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the Cordillera mountains by indigenous ancestors over two thousand years ago.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato are renowned for weaving T'nalak, a traditional cloth dyed with natural plant extracts.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial writing system that early Filipinos used to write on bamboo leaves and tree bark.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño with a distinctive two-step forward and one-step backward dance.
Dr. Gregorio Zara was a brilliant Filipino physicist who invented the two-way videophone and a solar-powered oven.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his masterpiece Spoliarium.
The Filipino tradition of bayanihan is famously demonstrated when community members carry a traditional nipa hut to help a family relocate.
Under Philippine law, the Commission on Elections ensures that every qualified citizen has the right to vote in national elections.
